details:
OrbitCare is an offline-first health monitoring web app for astronauts. It lets crew members check their own health, understand each reading in plain language, and know what to do next, whether they’re on the ISS, a spacecraft, the Moon or Mars.

What it does / how it works
Each astronaut has a profile with their personal Earth baselines. They log six health indicators by hand, or estimate heart rate with the device camera; that estimate runs entirely on-device and nothing is saved or sent. Every reading gets a green, yellow or red status, a one-sentence explanation and a clear next step. The app is organized around NASA’s five hazards of human spaceflight (RIDGE: Radiation, Isolation, Distance, Gravity, Environment), and each hazard has its own page:

Radiation: live NASA DONKI space weather (solar flares, solar energetic particles, geomagnetic storms and NASA alerts from the last 30 days). Each event is tagged by whether it matters at the crew’s current location. For example, a geomagnetic storm matters on the ISS but not on Mars.


Distance: the communication delay to Earth sets a response level. The further the crew is from Earth, the stricter the health limits get and the more self-reliant the guidance becomes.


Isolation: a memory bank of messages, photos, audio and video from home. If an astronaut logs low mood three check-ins in a row, the app surfaces a message from family.


Gravity and Environment: location-specific context, plus cabin sensor readings (CO₂ etc.). These sensors are simulated in our demo and clearly labelled as simulated.

The app also includes a master alarm for any red condition, emergency mode with five scenarios and a report to ground, a symptom checker, trend charts with range bands, daily check-in streaks, and an optional AI health assistant that can answer questions about the crew member’s vitals and history and read uploaded medical records.

Benefits and intended impact
On deep-space missions, real-time help from flight surgeons won’t always be possible: Mars has up to a 20-minute one-way delay. OrbitCare gives crews autonomy, so they can catch problems early and act on them without waiting for Earth. It is a guidance tool that supports flight surgeons; it doesn’t replace them.

Tools and technologies
JavaScript, React 19, Vite, Tailwind CSS v4, Recharts and React Router. The NASA DONKI API provides live space weather, and the Claude API powers the optional assistant. We used Claude Code as an AI coding assistant during development, and AI image tools for the logo and login background (disclosed in our README). All data is stored locally in the browser (localStorage and IndexedDB), with no backend, so the app works fully offline.

Creativity
Instead of a generic vitals dashboard, the app is structured around NASA’s own RIDGE framework. Its health limits adapt to how far the crew is from help, and it treats mental health as part of health monitoring by connecting low mood to messages from home.

Factors we considered
Offline use with no guaranteed connection; plain-language output for non-doctors under stress; personal baselines instead of one-size-fits-all ranges; privacy (camera data never leaves the device); and honesty in the interface, with simulated data always labelled and real NASA data marked LIVE or CACHED.
